channel.title: Parkers Physics — Recent Development
channel.description: New simulations, data sets, layers and fixes on Parkers Physics, as they ship — each with a link to open it.

item.title: EarthView's primary weather feed, back within its rate limit
item.description:
Every hourly weather update had been rejected for sending requests too fast, so EarthView fell back to a coarse 10° field. Requests are now paced across a few minutes and the full-resolution grid returns.

Open EarthView · Open System status

item.title: Launch Planner: the 3D stage no longer goes black
item.description:
On some graphics cards a single invalid pixel spread through the glow effect and blacked out the whole vehicle view. Those pixels are now filtered out, and the stage watches its own output and steps down its effects if a frame ever comes out black.

  • Links straight to a Falcon 9 or Starship launch now show that vehicle, not the Shuttle.
  • The "Next launches" strip fills in even when the launch feed arrives before the 3D view.
  • Now tested in Firefox and Safari's engine as well as Chrome.

Open Launch Planner

item.title: Earth Volcanoes lab
item.description:
All 2,661 Smithsonian GVP volcanoes on one page and as an EarthView layer, with live eruption status from USGS and NASA EONET, eruption odds, and a Monte-Carlo of volcanic climate forcing.

  • Status is a rule on the record — erupting, recent, historical, dormant, unconfirmed, inactive — never a guess.
  • Eruption odds are an empirical-Bayes onset rate fitted over every Holocene volcano, including the quiet ones.
  • A VEI-to-climate consequence calculator: Pinatubo through it gives −3.05 W m⁻² and −0.34 K.
  • If a live feed is down the page says "live status unavailable" — never a quiet planet.

Open Earth Volcanoes · Open EarthView · Volcanoes layer

item.title: Bulk weather and geomagnetic history moved to object storage
item.description:
Weather frames and sealed days of geomagnetic minute data are archived to R2, and the hourly temperature-extremes pass now runs in 0.04 s instead of 31–36 s.

Open System status

item.title: The Moon, lit by today's Sun
item.description:
The Moon page now runs on a live lunar ephemeris — phase, libration and terminator are today's — and gains a stagnant-lid mantle, a Monte-Carlo exosphere, and a Neukum crater field.

  • Phase, synodic age and distance in the HUD come from the same geometry that draws the terminator.
  • "Earth's view" puts the camera where you are standing tonight.
  • The interior reproduces the measured moment of inertia (0.3930 vs 0.3931).
  • Exosphere atoms hop, escape, photoionise and cold-trap — argon piles up before dawn, as observed.
  • Proposed colony sites and Earth-launch windows link straight into the Mission Planner.

Open The Moon · Open Lunar Colony · Open Mission Planner

item.title: Homepage Sun: flares, prominences, EUV waves — and the ten nearest NEOs
item.description:
Flares on the homepage Sun now release a field-aligned flow and launch EUV waves, prominences come from observed filament detections, and a new board lists the ten nearest near-Earth objects right now.

  • Every visual exaggeration on the Sun is printed in its legend.
  • The NEO board uses the same catalogue and propagator as the orrery and Near-Earth Watch.

Open Homepage

item.title: Jupiter Trojan population and proper elements
item.description:
A catalogue of Jupiter's Trojan asteroids integrated under the Sun, Jupiter and Saturn, with frequency-analysed proper elements validated against AstDyS.

Open Solar System

item.title: Earth–Moon gravity layer on Near-Earth Watch
item.description:
Lagrange points, Jacobi constants and a zero-velocity map in the live Earth–Moon frame, plus an acceleration budget for every tracked object.

Open Near-Earth Watch

item.title: Live JPL Horizons positions actually load now
item.description:
Every Horizons query had used a parameter the API rejects, so the orrery and space-weather pages had always fallen back to analytic positions. They now get the real ephemeris.

Open Solar System · Open Space Weather

item.title: Space Missions: the live fleet map
item.description:
Every active mission drawn from the best source available — JPL Horizons state vectors, then SGP4, then a labelled model — with upcoming launches and recent rocket bodies alongside.

  • Each marker says which source placed it.
  • L1 sentinels are visible for the first time — they used to sit inside the drawn Earth.

Open Space Missions

item.title: Launch Planner: a floodlit night pad
item.description:
The 3D vehicle view is now a floodlit night launch pad with simulated exhaust and deluge steam, bloom, and a camera that adapts to your screen shape.

Open Launch Planner

item.title: EarthView time scrubber: meteogram strip and smooth scrubbing
item.description:
A meteogram strip under the time slider with event markers, loop playback, and isobar contouring moved off the main thread — a scrub repaint went from 68 ms to 7 ms.

Open EarthView

item.title: EarthView: a physically lit globe and regional detail
item.description:
Sunlight now reddens through the real atmospheric path, the night side is dark, oceans glint with the live wind, and zooming into a region streams 2 km satellite cloud imagery.

  • Fixed: hovering or double-clicking the globe used to pick the point on the opposite side of the Earth.
  • "Go to a region" and shareable ?region= links.

Open EarthView

item.title: Wind colour: one palette across every altitude
item.description:
Brighter means faster and deeper means lower, on the globe and in every legend alike; dense wind no longer washes out to white.

Open EarthView

item.title: EarthView's live weather data is back
item.description:
The primary weather feed had been rejecting our requests for a month and every frame was a coarse fallback. Requests are now sized correctly, pressure is sea-level throughout, and stale data shows an amber marker.

Open EarthView · Open System status

item.title: Star Collider: gas drawn as kernels, HDR bloom
item.description:
Merger gas is now rendered as the SPH kernels themselves, with HDR bloom and new velocity, compression, mixing and shock views read straight from the engine.

Open Star Collider Lab

item.title: EarthView: tap a weekday for the whole day
item.description:
The verdict card's week strip opens a full-screen day view: hour-by-hour conditions, dayparts, and that night's sky and aurora odds.

Open EarthView

item.title: Orrery planets placed from the ephemeris
item.description:
Planets were placed on circles that were only right at page load — Mercury drifted 41° in a month. They now sit on their real ellipses at the simulation date.

Open Solar System

item.title: Public test sign-up and two-plan pricing
item.description:
Sign-up is open for testers, with simplified pricing and routing by what you came to do.

Open Pricing · Open Sign up

item.title: Orbital decay with time-varying solar drivers
item.description:
Decay forecasts now step through a day-by-day F10.7 and Ap schedule instead of holding today's values constant for the whole lifetime.

Open Operations

item.title: Storm-Season Fleet Assessment
item.description:
A sample assessment for satellite operators, with an interactive simulator of drag exposure across a storm season.

Open Sample Fleet Assessment

item.title: CME Outlook: seven-day eruption probability
item.description:
The chance of an Earth-arriving CME on each of the next seven days, from eruptions that have not happened yet — each visible region's flare odds flown through the flux-rope engine.

  • Days three and beyond are lower bounds, and say so.
  • Scored daily against what actually arrives.

Open CME Forecast

item.title: TIGA: Sun and Moon geospace layer
item.description:
The magnetopause and bow shock drawn on the live L1 solar wind, with the Moon's monthly passage through Earth's magnetotail.

Open TIGA · Geomagnetic

item.title: Boötes Void: galaxy tracker, N-body forecast, force probe
item.description:
Probe the void's gravity at any point, follow its galaxies through cosmic time, and run a 35,000-particle N-body forecast and reconstruction in your browser.

Open Boötes Void

item.title: Flux-rope forecasts scored on real arrivals
item.description:
The daily CME forecast ledger is scored only on forecasts locked before each shock arrived, against real L1 data — the published skill numbers are now an honest record.

Open CME Forecast · Open Compounding Watch

item.title: Upper Atmosphere: a stage you can arrange
item.description:
Every panel over the 3D view is a movable, resizable window, and operational altitude bands (VLEO, station, constellation, SSO) are drawn as a ruler you can click.

Open Upper Atmosphere

item.title: CME data restored after NASA moved DONKI
item.description:
NASA moved its DONKI service and the old addresses began returning a web page instead of data. All CME, flare and notification feeds now use the new host with a fallback.

Open Compounding Watch · Open Space Weather

item.title: Near-Earth objects drawn at their real size
item.description:
Asteroids are lit and sized from published photometry, become 3D rocks when they resolve on screen, and meteor showers are drawn as parallel streaks.

Open Solar System

item.title: Space-weather notifications show NASA's real text
item.description:
DONKI notifications were sometimes rendered as a bare "##" heading. They now show the message NASA actually published, or nothing at all.

Open Space Weather

item.title: Privacy Policy v3.0, Terms v1.3, and a DPA
item.description:
Updated privacy and terms pages covering location, analytics and retention, plus a Data Processing Agreement for organisations.

Open Privacy Policy · Open Terms of Service · Open Data Processing Agreement

item.title: Orrery: let go of a locked body
item.description:
A clear way to deselect a planet, moon or asteroid and return to the free camera, with panels that no longer misjudge their own size.

Open Solar System

item.title: Space Ship Designer: real-size engines and a guided ascent
item.description:
Engines are built at their published sizes, each design flies its own optimised two-burn ascent at true scale with winds aloft, and the result card charts the climb.

Open Space Ship Designer

item.title: Planetary Temperature Lab: 1991–2020 normals
item.description:
Climate normals for every grid cell, so "unusually hot" can be measured against the calendar rather than against last month.

Open System status

item.title: SkyView: your sky, right now
item.description:
A real-time sky chart for your location that ranks the ten things you can actually see tonight, with a 30-night forecast of the best nights.

Open SkyView

item.title: Satellite Designer: build a spacecraft that closes
item.description:
Pick a bus and subsystems from a component library, see them placed in 3D, and get an engineering review of mass, power, thermal and drag budgets.

Open Satellite Designer

item.title: Upper Atmosphere: satellite suites and orbit rings
item.description:
Toggle families of real satellites with their orbit rings and an altitude ladder, on the same clock as the atmosphere.

Open Upper Atmosphere

item.title: Upper Atmosphere: camera rig and incoming CMEs
item.description:
Pan, swivel, change lens and frame any layer edge-on from the limb — and watch an incoming CME's flux rope approach Earth.

Open Upper Atmosphere

item.title: Upper Atmosphere: fly through the thermosphere
item.description:
A flight-dynamics layer with gravity, J2 and drag against the rotating air, and one consistent Earth-fixed frame for the Sun, bulge and satellites.

Open Upper Atmosphere

item.title: Mars 3D now runs in Firefox
item.description:
A script-ordering bug had stopped the Mars 3D engine starting in Firefox for seven weeks.

Open Real-Time Mars

item.title: Mars: an explorable map, and the right season
item.description:
A searchable feature index, a top-down map view, zoom-through to the surface, and a season computed correctly from JPL.

Open Real-Time Mars

item.title: Climate Lab dashboard
item.description:
Your account dashboard is now an instrument bench: a home weather station, meteogram, alert console and satellite pass tracker.

Open Dashboard

item.title: Homepage: the Sun's next 24 hours
item.description:
The homepage opens on today's Sun — real NOAA active regions — and plays the next 24 hours of CMEs through the flux-rope engine.

Open Homepage

item.title: Homepage: today's Earth and NOAA's aurora
item.description:
The homepage globe is NASA imagery turned to today's sunlight and season, with the live OVATION aurora oval on the real magnetic dipole.

Open Homepage

item.title: EarthView clouds follow the clock
item.description:
Scrubbing time now shows archived satellite cloud frames for that moment, a wind-advected nowcast just ahead, and model-only clouds further out.

Open EarthView

item.title: Homepage 30-day temperature outlook
item.description:
A daily-candle temperature chart and a 30-day calendar for your location, relaxing from the forecast toward the local normal.

Open Homepage
